newsitem.title: UK: Southern Electric profits slip, mulls payout.
newsitem.headline: Southern Electric profits slip, mulls payout.

text.p: British regional electricity company Southern Electric Plc said Thursday it plans to return about 180 million pounds ($302.2 million) to shareholders as it posted an expected dip in first-half profits.
The cash-rich electricity supplier's pretax profits slid to 112.2 million pounds ($188.4 million) in the six months to Sept. 30 from 118.7 million pounds ($199.3 million) in the year-ago period.
The results, sapped by mandatory distribution price cuts that took effect in April, fell within analysts' forecast range of 102 million ($171.3 million) to 120 million pounds ($201.5 million).
"Our operating profit was up 6.5 percent, despite the impact of the price review which is cutting distribution revenue," finance director Ian Marchant said in an interview.
The company, which operates in central southern England, plans to return about 10 percent of the value of its share capital to shareholders by March 1997.

Possible options included a share buyback or a special dividend, Marchant said. "We're looking at a number of ways that we can achieve that efficiently and fairly and expect to make an announcement in the next couple of weeks."

Southern boosted its half year dividend to 12.9 pence (21.7 cents) from 11.3p (19 cents) per share and said it planned a total dividend of 43 pence (72.2 cents) per share for the year, up 10 percent from last year.
The company predicts it will keep growing dividends by 5 percent to 8 percent in real terms until the year 2000.
Southern's shares were unchanged at 687.5 pence ($11.54) at midday as its earnings, outlook and plans to reduce its cash mountain failed to impress the market.

"The operating profits increased, but not massively. And the dividend was high, but still there's more they can do with their cash," said analyst Simon Champion at Charterhouse Tilney. "Even after the return of value, they're still going to be sitting on a lot of cash."
Southern, whose attempts to tie up with its neighbouring water company Southern Water and generating giant National Power have been foiled, said it has no further plans for mergers or acquisitions.
"Given the (regulatory) environment and the political scene we're facing, we do not believe that a deal is currently feasible for us," Marchant said.

"But we do not need to do a deal. We've got good growth prospects in all our core businesses and we're committed to growing organically," he added, noting the company plans to invest 700 million pounds ($1.2 billion) over five years in its network.

Southern Electic's expansion plans include boosting its supply business and making additional investments in two generation plants. Proposals for another three generation sites in its region were well advanced, Marchant said.
The company expects to agree early next year to an electricity supply deal that would be similar to its recent 15-year agreement with nuclear power generator British Energy Plc, he said.
The company said it planned further price reductions for domestic customers from April of next year.
